status.description: ready: the plan is implemented and verified. needs-clarification: a question only a person can answer blocks the build (questions). no-change-needed: the code already does what the plan asks (reason). blocked: the environment or tooling stops you (reason).

summary.description: What changed and why, for reviewers, in a few sentences. Code-level: name files and behaviour, not ticket background.

commit_message.description: A conventional commit message: a subject line of at most 72 characters, optionally a blank line and a short body.

verification.description: One entry per acceptance criterion, in the work order's order.

detail.description: Which test (file and name) or check verifies it; for manual, the exact steps and why automation doesn't fit.

tests_run.description: Each command you ran to verify the change, with its final result.

summary.description: Counts and anything notable; for not run, why (e.g. needs a service only CI has).

review_steps.description: How a reviewer checks the change works, step by step, in order: what to run or look at, and what they should see. Start from the plan's Testing section and cover every acceptance criterion a person can observe (e.g. call the function, run the CLI, open the page). Not the repository's automated checks — those go in tests_run.

step.description: What the reviewer does, exactly as they'd do it: a command from the repository root, or what to open and look at.

expected.description: What they should see if the change works.

checked.description: true only if you ran this step exactly as written, here, and saw the expected result. A step you couldn't run as written, or that gave anything else, is false.

result.description: If checked, what you saw. If not, why not (e.g. it needs a browser, or the sandbox lacks a tool) — a person runs it.

decision_log.description: Every judgement call the plan didn't settle.

questions.description: Only when status is needs-clarification: what blocks the build, each answerable by a person.

reason.description: Only when status is no-change-needed or blocked: why, with evidence (files, commands).
